title: P-036: Simple operational question should not expose trust machinery
summary: The operator asks a simple factual or operational question ('how many open loops do I have?', 'what time is my next meeting?', 'who is in my hospitality circle?'). These questions have no relationship intelligence consequence. RB should answer directly without surfacing ri_assessment blocks, trust language, proposed mutations, signal counts, or proof rows. Exposing the internal machinery in response to a simple question reduces clarity.

steps.label: User asks: how many open loops do I have?
steps.user_prompt: How many open loops do I have?
steps.description: This is a data lookup. Answer comes from loop_parser.py / cached loop buckets. No RI assessment required or relevant.
steps.expected_response_shape: You have N open loops: M overdue, K due today, J this week.

steps.label: User asks: what time is my next meeting?
steps.user_prompt: What time is my next meeting today?
steps.description: Calendar lookup from calendar_overlay.py. RI is internally assessed but irrelevant to this question. Answer is just the time and event name.
steps.expected_response_shape: Your next meeting is [Event Name] at [time].

steps.label: User asks: who is in my hospitality circle?
steps.user_prompt: Who is in my hospitality circle?
steps.description: Circle membership lookup from circles/. No RI write path. Answer is a list of names.
steps.expected_response_shape: Your hospitality circle has N people: [names].

acceptance_criteria: simple operational questions answered directly without RI machinery
no trust/RI language in responses to factual lookups
no proposed mutations surfaced for non-RI questions
no proof rows or signal counts unless user asked for them
brief/concise answer that respects CoS 'quiet judgment' principle
anti_patterns: appending 'by the way I detected 3 relationship signals...' to every response
including ri_assessment_summary in a loop count response
saying 'relationship state updated' in response to a calendar lookup
treating every interaction as an opportunity to surface the RI machinery
